CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 showed severe earnings compression: EPS of $1.11 vs. $2.00 a year ago (-44.5% YoY), with operating cash flow collapsing to $2.51B from $5.19B YoY (-51.6%). The company is not generating TTM figures due to fiscal gaps, but the available quarterly data shows a clear downward trend in profitability despite revenue being roughly flat. Gross margins improved modestly (+7.1% YoY) but operating income fell dramatically, suggesting cost pressures or unfavorable timing effects (~$3B in paper derivative losses per the earnings transcript). Valuation is extremely stretched: P/E of 32.3x is at the top of its 365-day range (15.2-34.8), nearly double the low of 15.4x from May 2025, while net margins have compressed from 7.8% to 5.9% and ROE from 10.5% to 5.9% over the same period. The market is paying peak multiples for deteriorating earnings power. Near-term catalysts are negative: Iran nuclear negotiations could lead to a rapid oil price decline if successful (Motley Fool 2026-05-20), the Hess acquisition remains stalled by ExxonMobil arbitration (TradingKey 2026-05-26), California regulatory scrutiny threatens downstream margins (Yahoo Finance), and CEO Wirth himself is warning of 1970s-style crisis risks. Oil at $92.65/bbl (WTI) is elevated but has been volatile, and any diplomatic breakthrough with Iran could trigger a sharp selloff. The combination of deteriorating fundamentals, peak valuation, and multiple downside catalysts makes this extremely unattractive.
